A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAC research and contain readable main text and Appendices A–G. Matching text, equations, tables, and rendered figures supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original transportation and image-generation experiments, including ablations and hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experimental results, including transportation distances, generation metrics, ablations, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: MAC's diagonal coefficients, sinusoidal parameterization, optional pretraining, adversarial objectives, and inference solver are retained. Tensor-axis notation changes do not establish an architectural or procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian/Moons transportation tasks and CIFAR-10, ImageNet-32/64, FFHQ-64, and AFHQv2-64 generation tasks, with the same conditional and unconditional settings.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the corresponding experiments. Lu et al. (2023), newly mentioned in the related-work paragraph, already appears as the CD_alpha + adv_theta comparator in v3's Table 5.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, sampling procedures, metrics, and evaluation sample counts remain unchanged. Appendix F specifies the same 50,000 generated samples for metric computation.

E4.justification: The conditioning and joint-training ablations, multidimensionality tests, coefficient visualizations, hyperparameter sweeps, and trajectory-linearity analysis are retained with identical evidence in Tables 4 and 6, Figures 6–8 and 10, and Appendix E.

E5.justification: Appendix E.1.2 still reports means and standard deviations across three seeds. Appendix F retains three runs with different seeds and reporting of the minimum FID and FD_DINOv2.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and generated samples are unchanged, including appendix results. Table 5 retains conditional CIFAR-10 FID 1.37 and ImageNet-64 FID 1.48 and FD_DINOv2 70.2 under the same settings.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, parameterization equations, and solver derivations retain their mathematical substance. Adding the gradient subscript x, permuting tensor-axis notation, and reordering channel-count factors are equivalent notational clarifications.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: multidimensional adaptive trajectory control, efficient adversarial optimization, and evaluating trajectory optimality through final transportation quality.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning nonstraight trajectories, joint optimization, and label-dependent coefficients remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning fixed NFE and conditioning only on the starting point.

D1.justification: Implementation configurations, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and codebase references are retained. Table 7's new adversarial-training qualifier repeats the budget scope already documented in v3's Appendix E.3.2 and Table 15.

R1.justification: Section 2 broadens its few-step-generation framing from diffusion distillation to distillation and fine-tuning, and includes Lu et al. (2023) in that discussion. This is a limited positioning refinement; the bibliography and principal novelty distinction remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 locally rewrites the few-step-generation related-work paragraph and training-efficiency discussion, and standardizes gradient and tensor-axis notation across the main text and appendices. The overall section organization is preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 5 and Table 7 are repositioned within their pages, with accompanying text reflow and spacing adjustments. Table 7's caption now specifies adversarial training. Figures, plots, table entries, and appendix sample displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly improves clarity through standardized tensor-axis notation, more explicit distillation/fine-tuning framing, and Table 7's adversarial-training caption. These refinements reduce ambiguity while preserving the same scientific evidence and limitations.
